prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent RGBA sprite atlas for an elaborate paper pop-up Pokémon Emerald terrarium. 1536x1024 landscape, 4 columns by 3 rows, exactly twelve isolated objects. Keep generous transparent gutters and complete silhouettes.
Style: carefully hand-cut colored paper illustration, many thin overlapping paper layers, cream cut edges, subtle fiber grain, charming detailed flat stage props. Front view with slight top visibility. No sculpted 3D, no glossy plastic, no photorealism. No ground patches, no backdrop, no printed labels or text, no grid, no exterior shadows. True transparency.
Row 1 left to right: maritime museum anchor on a small dark wood display plinth, rope loop around anchor; spiral ammonite fossil mounted upright on a blue velvet square exhibit stand; miniature white ocean research ship with blue trim and two tiny masts on a dark wooden cradle; low museum information lectern with a cream map drawing of island outlines, no lettering.
Row 2 left to right: compact tournament trophy with gold cup and blue ribbons on a small wooden square pedestal; two red velvet posts joined by a single elegant gold rope; low woven wicker planter with pink flowers and layered emerald leaves; a short stack of three colorful gym practice cushions, cobalt blue, red and ochre, visibly folded paper cloth texture.
Row 3 left to right: small wooden judges desk with a closed cream notebook and a tiny blue desk bell; a standalone round brass ship's bell hanging under a short horizontal dark wood crossbar, no supporting stand; a single three-loop pink-blue paper streamer ribbon isolated for celebratory falling animation; an open blue-and-gold folding paper hand fan, no hand, with alternating layered pleats and tiny white flower motifs.
Each prop must have many readable little paper construction details and clean silhouette, not one generic blob. Objects are independent movable stage cards. Museum props in muted navy, warm wood, cream and brass; tournament props festive red, blue, gold, green.
